institutionRules.title: There are no required courses for admission to Stanford
institutionRules.detail: Stanford states outright: "There are no required courses for admission to Stanford," and it "cannot provide specific guidance on course selection."

institutionRules.title: You apply to the university, not a major
institutionRules.detail: "When you apply to Stanford, you apply to the university as a whole, not to a particular major, department, or school. As a result, there are no additional requirements for certain areas of study."

institutionRules.title: The strongest applicants have two years of college-level work
institutionRules.detail: Stanford has no minimum credits or years, but its most competitive applicants have the equivalent of two years of college-level coursework by entry, in consecutive years of full-time, IN-PERSON study, and are typically in their second year when applying.

institutionRules.title: At most 90 QUARTER units transfer
institutionRules.detail: Incoming transfer students may transfer a maximum of 90 quarter units — roughly two years — regardless of units earned at previous institutions. At least two years of full-time enrollment at Stanford are required for the degree.

institutionRules.title: C- or better, substantially similar, no duplication
institutionRules.detail: Stanford has NO articulation agreements with any college. A course generally transfers if it is at an accredited institution, substantially similar to a Stanford course, completed with a minimum grade of C- or Pass (where Pass equals C- or above), does not duplicate or regress prior coursework, and was not used toward high school graduation requirements.

institutionRules.title: Some departments and GE requirements accept no online courses
institutionRules.detail: Extension, correspondence, and online credit transfers only if the offering university allows it toward its own degree.

institutionRules.title: A lifetime limit of three Stanford undergraduate applications
institutionRules.detail: Students are limited to a total of three applications for undergraduate admission, first-year and transfer combined.

institutionRules.title: ACT or SAT test scores are required
institutionRules.detail: Also required: Common Application by March 15, $100 fee, official high school transcript with graduation date, official transcripts from every college, the College Report, and letters of recommendation from two academic instructors. Decision by mid-May; reply June 1.

institutionRules.detail: Students who at the time of entry will have completed at least two terms of study with high academic standing at an accredited institution may apply. In your first year of college, the earliest you can apply is during your second term.

institutionRules.title: More than five terms may make you ineligible
institutionRules.detail: Students who at entry will have completed more than two and a half years — five terms or semesters — of college may not be eligible because of MIT's residency requirements.

institutionRules.title: One application per entry year
institutionRules.detail: Applying to enter in the spring term bars reapplying for the fall term of the same calendar year.

institutionRules.title: MIT does not award second bachelor's degrees
institutionRules.detail: Even for a different field of study.

institutionRules.title: No minimum GPA, but admits hold 3.5+ with mostly A's in math and science
institutionRules.detail: "There is no minimum required GPA, but competitive applicants generally have a GPA of 3.5 or above, and mostly A's in mathematics and science courses."

institutionRules.title: Transfers typically lose at least a semester and enter as sophomores
institutionRules.detail: "Transfer students typically lose at least one semester of coursework, and most students enter MIT as sophomores — regardless of the amount of coursework they completed at their previous institutions." Credit is assessed only after admission, by the relevant academic departments; where the record does not merit credit you may sit an Advanced Standing Examination.

institutionRules.title: SAT or ACT required, taken by a hard date
institutionRules.detail: MIT requires the SAT or ACT (no ACT writing/science, no SAT essay). Tests must be taken by October 31 for spring entry and before March 31 for fall entry. All sittings must be reported; MIT superscores by section.

institutionRules.title: Two college recommendations, one from a math or science instructor
institutionRules.detail: Spring entry (February) applications are due October 15 and are open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents only. Fall entry (September) applications are due March 1; financial aid applications are due February 15. Materials: the MIT Transfer Application form ($75), all secondary school and college transcripts, two academic letters of recommendation from college instructors — one must be from a math or science instructor — and a School Official Report.
